newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Baltic business newspapers plan pan-Baltic index.
newsitem.headline: Baltic business newspapers plan pan-Baltic index.

text.p: The three main business newspapers of Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania are to launch a Baltic share index in May, Estonian newspaper Aripaev said on Thursday.
The index will be the first to track the leading shares of the three young stock markets on a pan-Baltic basis.
Baltic shares have been attracting increasing interest both from abroad and from local players. Estonia in particular has attracted much foreign attention as it has a liquid market.
Estonian Aripaev, Latvian Dienas Bizness and Lithuanian Verslo Zinios will choose 10 leading stock market companies with the highest capitalisation from each country for the index.
"The index will give an overall picture not only of Estonia but of the whole Baltic stock market," Aripaev senior editor Andrus Vaher told Reuters.
"The word 'Baltics' is more familiar to international investors than the three countries separately," he added.
The three newspapers, part of the Swedish Bonnier empire, also plan to launch a fund in all Baltic countries, similar to the Aripaev Index Fund launched a month ago, he added.
Aripaev launched an Estonian index in April 1995. Since then, it has risen by around eight times.
The Lithuanian and Estonian share markets already have their own in-house indices and the Latvian market is expected to launch an index later this year.
